cells.tense: You are here with the question, and it has not closed.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Once you've asked and listened, take the next step while the question stays open. One step, taken today, with no proof required first.
cells.core:
Here, before anything has been chosen, you can ask into what isn't known. You turn a thing over, catch what nobody has said, and sit in the not-knowing long enough for something accurate to land. That is the good version: a perception arrives without argument, and the question stays open while it does. When it bends, the same asking has no floor under it — it circles back to what you already think and closes early.

What this balance is free to feed next is a decisive act taken with a question still open. Once you've asked and listened, take the next step while the question stays open — one step, taken today, with no proof required first. The walking is the point; the answer was not the condition. A step like that shows your asking what it is for.

cells.tense: You will have settled the answer before anyone has spoken the question.
cells.act: ask the beginner's question about where to go
cells.ask: Ask where to go as if you were just starting, with nothing prepared, and carry the question open into tomorrow.
cells.core:
Where nothing has been chosen yet, you close questions before anything has landed. They get answered before they are asked, the ground reads as mapped when it isn't, and people have stopped bringing you the half-formed things they used to. The freshness is doing something — it is running past what anyone can see — and what comes back to you is thinner than what you send out. The bend is not a flaw in the asking. It is the asking arriving too early to hear anything.

What turns this around is moving with no destination in hand. Ask where to go as if you were just starting, with nothing prepared, and carry the question open into tomorrow. That is a beginner's move, not a finisher's. The only question that can still teach you is one you haven't answered, and an open question overnight costs nothing real.

cells.tense: A question you stopped asking has not moved from where you left it.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Picture the next small thing you want, then take its first step this week without waiting to feel ready.
cells.core:
Before any choice is made here, a question you stopped asking hasn't moved. You watch other people ask and get answers, and the not-knowing that used to be easy in you has gone quiet. Asking into what isn't known got set down, and picking it back up alone feels like reaching across distance. Something startles the perception out now and then, and it lands clean, which is a small piece of evidence you can hold.

What refills this is imagining ahead of what is sensible. Picture the next small thing you want, then take its first step this week without waiting to feel ready. The picture is allowed to be unfinished; that is what it is for. Energy comes back through the wanted thing rather than through demanding more of the empty question, so follow what has some pull. The ground is not gone. It is untrodden.

cells.tense: The room is already moving to your questions, and you say you were just there.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Next time a feeling runs hot, write one line of what it asks of you against what it gives, and make the next move from that line.
cells.core:
With nothing chosen yet, your questions are already steering things. Somewhere in the last stretch, asking into what isn't known started setting what rooms do next — people come to you for a read on the thing — and your own account has you merely asking, merely curious. The curious part is true. What is missing is that it changed outcomes, and no one had a reason to point that out.

What returns the pen here is judging one feeling fairly. Next time a feeling runs hot, write one line of what it asks of you against what it gives, and make the next move from that line. The line puts your hand back on a lever that was already being pulled. You don't owe anyone an announcement; you owe the next move a fair weighing, done by you.

attempts.check: The one thing the record does not support is why the Too Little person is standing at the door: I do not know what happened there, so the cell locates the stance and says nothing about its cause, duration or cost. A reader could reasonably say the Too Much cell assumes they are performing for an audience they haven't named, so the line stays on the bending — deciding ahead of any information — and never on motive. The asks survive being wrong: dropping a condition, sitting the class once, taking the unaimed walk, and writing a line between what a feeling asks and what it gets are all doable and teach something even if the read misses. The sentence that serves me more than them — that the fresh curiosity is 'still intact' — I cut; the record does not certify intactness, only what the capacity is doing now.
